hints.title: Constant-Time Random Sampling and Removal
hints.text: Generating an element with equal probability in constant time requires contiguous array indexing, while O(1) membership checks require index mapping. How can swapping to the back enable constant-time removal from an array?

hints.title: Dynamic Array with Index Dictionary
hints.text: Pair a dynamic array storing values with a dictionary mapping val to its current index in the array. Insert appends to the array and records the index.

hints.title: Swap with Last Element on Deletion
hints.text: To delete val in O(1) time without shifting elements, retrieve its index, overwrite it with the array last element, update the moved element index in the dictionary, and pop from the back.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.time: O(1) average for insert, remove, and getRandom
variables: N: number of elements currently stored in the set
complexity.notes: Swap-with-last element technique turns O(N) array shift deletions into O(1) pop operations.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Array removal costs O(N) due to element shifting; hash sets do not support uniform random index sampling in O(1) without arrays.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Dual array + dictionary storage coordinates O(1) indexed sampling and O(1) lookups.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Handling removal when the element to delete is already the last element in the array without corrupting dictionary state.
